[Hacker News — anthropic.com]
Our charter is to responsibly develop and maintain advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. Anthropic is a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC), a designation that requires us to balance the financial interests of shareholders with the benefit to the broader public. Our Public Benefit Report takes stock of what we are doing to serve the public benefit, and of the work ahead. Read our 2026 Public Benefit Report Pillar 1 The technical problems of AI safety are solved. Powerful AI can be developed and deployed without severe, irreversible harms. Read more Pillar 2 AI safety is a universal practice backstopped by law. AI developers everywhere follow safe development and deployment practices, sustained by industry norms and enforced by regulation. Read more Pillar 3 AI strengthens democracy and global stability. Democracies hold the lead in AI and use it to better serve the public and promote peace. Read more Pillar 4 AI expands prosperity and human flourishing. AI enables unprecedented economic growth, and the resulting prosperity empowers every person to pursue a good life. Read more Pillar 5 AI’s benefits are shared by everyone. AI delivers transformative benefits that reach people everywhere, and the opportunities AI creates are distributed. Read more Explore the work Learn more about our research, policies, and programs. We plan to add to this record over time. Building advanced AI in a way that is safe, trustworthy, and accountable to the people it affects isn’t a niche concern or a competitive differentiator. It is a necessary step toward making the benefits real. We’re already seeing what’s possible—in research labs, in classrooms, and in the everyday work of people solving hard problems. If we get this right, I believe that some of humanity’s greatest moments await us on the other side. Daniela Amodei Co-Founder and President, Anthropic Read our 2026 Public Benefit Report

[Hacker News] Maybe you're thinking of B Corp? That's just a certification from some group. Public Benefit Corporation, on the other hand, changes directors' fiduciary responsibilities. For example, earlier this year, the Delaware Court of Chancery ruled that PBC directors are not obligated to maximize shareholder value when selling control of their company.
